A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CGLS research work. All 15 pages of v1 and 16 pages of v2, including their appendices, are readable; the text, equations, tables, and rendered figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original compute-matched pretraining experiments at GPT-2-Small and Llama-3.2-1B scales, including downstream accuracy, perplexity, starting-depth comparisons, and MMLU analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original pretraining results and adds 20B-token training, code-domain transfer, few-shot evaluation, replicated runs, and training-stage analyses.

M1.justification: The curriculum mixture, progressive addition of randomly initialized layers, frozen-weight initialization phase, and subsequent full-model tuning are unchanged. Defaulting to the previously evaluated half-depth configuration and clarifying MIDAS implementation do not introduce a new CGLS procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds a general-web-to-Python-code training scenario using DCLM and StarCoder2, evaluated on HumanEval (Section 5.1, Table 3). It removes MMLU evaluation, including the STEM column and full appendix breakdown. The 20B-token experiment expands training scale within existing DCLM coverage.

E2.justification: The main comparison retains the randomized and curricularized baselines, layer-scaling-only, MIDAS, and pretrained references. Locally, the starting-depth comparison changes: v1 Table 4 includes a randomized-baseline reference, whereas the replacement depth-sweep plot in v2 Figure 2 shows only CGLS configurations.

E3.justification: v2 adds 20B-token training and a 4B-token code-transfer experiment with HumanEval pass@8/16/32/64 evaluation. Appendix A.2 introduces matched zero- and five-shot evaluations using PMI accuracy. The retained main experiments preserve their settings, but their 1B aggregate now excludes MMLU. Figure 2 inconsistently labels the depth-sweep budget as 2B tokens in its title and 2.5B in its caption.

E4.justification: v2 expands the existing starting-depth analysis with 4- and 12-layer starts, adds a final-stage budget sweep, and reports validation trajectories across training stages (Figures 2 and 5). It also tests general-text-to-code distribution shift. The MMLU category analysis is removed; the existing per-domain perplexity plots are retained rather than newly added.

E5.justification: v1 provides no repeated-run counts or uncertainty estimates. v2 Table 7 newly reports three training runs per method at the 1B/2.5B-token scale, with means and standard errors; Appendix A.4 discusses the higher variability of CGLS. This establishes new uncertainty reporting without establishing an increase from a known earlier run count.

E6.justification: Shared main-table task scores and existing perplexity plots are unchanged. New results include 20B-token average accuracy of 42.30% for CGLS versus 38.41% for the randomized baseline, and HumanEval pass@8 of 6.67% versus 3.56% (v2 Tables 2–3), plus few-shot, replication, and trajectory results. MMLU and some configuration-specific entries disappear. Changed main-table 1B averages reflect removal of MMLU, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The curriculum-mixture definition and parameter-transfer equation remain unchanged, with no added or revised theorems, proofs, or derivations. Removing the standard PMI scoring formula alongside the MMLU description changes evaluation exposition, not substantive mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract and central claim about synchronizing curriculum and model growth remain stable. However, the introduction and discussion extend the contribution to 20B-token training and domain-adaptive code pretraining, beyond v1's low-budget experiments. MMLU-STEM-specific claims are removed, and the reported average advantage is revised for the reduced benchmark set.

C2.justification: v2 adds a depth-related inductive-bias explanation for the perplexity/downstream-performance discrepancy and qualifies that discrepancy by training budget. It interprets new stage trajectories, seed variability, and code-transfer results in terms of knowledge transfer, stability, and domain adaptation. The MMLU-subfield interpretations disappear, while the existing half-depth recommendation remains.

D1.justification: v2 adds MIDAS weight-copying clarification, the code-transfer mixture schedule, and measured training times on four H100s: 5h53m for CGLS versus 5h39m for the baseline. Existing optimizer, learning-rate, and hardware details remain. It removes dataset/model license disclosures and the GPT-2 three-layer-start curriculum weights, although that configuration remains in the perplexity plot.

R1.justification: v2 adds Du et al. on stacking, Heineman and Hwang et al. on evaluation practice, Ouyang et al. on fine-tuning, and two Tay et al. studies supporting the depth/perplexity discussion. The MMLU reference is removed. The central positioning as a combination of curriculum learning and progressive model growth is unchanged.

P1.justification: Most abstract, introduction, method, and setup wording is retained. v2 promotes related work to a separate section, simplifies CGLS configuration names, edits results and discussion, and reorganizes the appendices around the expanded analyses. The MMLU, broader-impact, and licensing sections are removed, without an extensive rewrite of the retained exposition.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document template, headers, typography, and citation presentation. It relocates curriculum tables and existing perplexity plots, removes the MMLU table, replaces the depth-comparison table with plots, and adds four experimental tables plus budget/depth and stage-trajectory figures. Table 4's caption still describes the omitted three-layer-start configuration.

improvement.justification: v1's evidence was confined to low-token-budget experiments without reported run-to-run uncertainty. v2 tests the method at 20B tokens and under code-domain transfer, adds three-run uncertainty estimates, and directly examines budget allocation and learning trajectories. These address important gaps in generality and reliability. Removing MMLU detail and licensing information reduces transparency, and appendix inconsistencies remain, but the expanded validation substantially strengthens the paper's empirical foundation.
